subject: KMS/SSO carveout governance & temporary keystore path
messages:
From: Lauren Price <l.price@medspring.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Medspring Security <security@medspring.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary keystore path & audit evidence for BYOK requirement

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the runthrough yesterday. To recap from our side: Medspring needs a short-term path to meet our SOC2/BYOK requirement while we wait for a full Private deployment (estimated 4–6 months). Specifically we need:

- A documented temporary keystore option (customer-managed key material that never leaves our control) for hosted/Dedicated customers while we evaluate Private.
- Audit log evidence showing key usage, access events, and immutable export for our internal auditors.
- Clear retention guarantees (we're proposing 90 days for the initial phase) and a mechanism to escrow rotated keys for forensics.

Can Redwood provide an interim design and proposed timeline for a POC? We don't want to block rollout but need something we can show to compliance by end of November. Attaching a short compliance summary from our side.

Appreciate any appetite for a short carveout/exception path.

—Lauren
Medspring Health — Senior Security Program Manager

Attachments: msp_compliance_summary.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Price <l.price@medspring.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary keystore path & audit evidence for BYOK requirement

Thanks Lauren — looping in team to triage. Quick internal ask list below so we can align on scope and owners: 

1) Policy decision: temporary "customer-keystore proxy" vs full BYOK in hosted. Which security guarantees do we insist on (immutable logs, proof-of-wipe, escrow)?
2) Retention: Lauren suggests 90d for POC. Do we accept or propose our standard enterprise baseline (we usually default to 180d unless otherwise negotiated)?
3) SSO handshake: Medspring will require assertion-level audit events. Need engineering to confirm event surface.
4) Implementation timeline & owner: Ideally a POC in 2–3 weeks so Laurel can present something to auditors.

Ben/Neha/Priyom/Grace — can each comment inline on ownership/feasibility? I'll consolidate and send a short RFC to Lauren and their security team.

Marissa
Director, Product — Security & Compliance (Redwood Inference)

Attachment: draft_exception_policy.md (placeholder)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Lauren Price <l.price@medspring.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary keystore path & audit evidence for BYOK requirement

Quick technical read from SecOps: we can offer a temporary keystore proxy that does not export raw key material to Redwood-managed storage. Notes/constraints:

- Auditability: must emit key usage events (key-id, operation, timestamp, actor) to an immutable write-once export (we can push to a tenant-owned S3 with object lock + retention).
- Escrow: for forensic needs, propose a sealed-blob escrow where Medspring receives the wrap-key; rotation events create new sealed blobs stored in escrow.
- Retention: 90 days is acceptable for a POC but we need a signed exception if we deviate from our 180d default. 90d increases legal/custodial risk; flagging to Legal if auditors push beyond POC window.
- SSO: we can surface assertion-level events but will need minor changes in the identity layer to correlate SAML/SCIM events with key ops.

I'll take Security lead if Marissa confirms. I'll draft an audit_matrix_v2.xlsx mapping required evidence -> implementation ticket.

Ben
Security Ops Manager

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Lauren Price <l.price@medspring.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary keystore path & audit evidence for BYOK requirement

Thanks — engineering notes and minimal-viable-architecture (MVA) for POC: 

1) Design: a thin proxy layer that accepts Medspring-provided wrap keys via an HSM-backed envelope. Runtime never persists plaintext keys; envelope unwrap only within ephemeral memory. We log key-id + operation + request-id. POC will be single-tenant on Dedicated nodes.

2) SSO correlation: we will add a correlation id in the token handler so SAML assertion IDs are recorded in key event logs. That requires a ~2 day change in identity middleware + tests.

3) Console & API: Add a flag "temporary_customer_keystore" in console and SDK. This requires product/UX sign-off and a small UI flow for granting escrow consent.

4) Timeline & milestones (provisional):
   - RFC & security checklist by 2027-10-27 (owner: Priyom)
   - Engineering spike & PoC build (Neha) 2027-10-28 -> 2027-11-10
   - SecOps validation & audit export tests (Ben) 2027-11-11 -> 2027-11-17

5) Known unknowns: cost delta for Dedicated tenancy and S3 ObjectLock escrow costs; rollback behavior for key revocation needs product-facing text.

Attaching initial design doc: temp_keystore_design_v1.pdf

Neha
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Price <l.price@medspring.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary keystore path & audit evidence for BYOK requirement

Thanks team — this is actionable. Summary and next steps for Lauren and Medspring: 

- Decision: proceed with a temporary keystore proxy POC scoped to Dedicated tenancy. We accept 90d retention for the POC with a signed exception; default enterprise baseline remains 180d.
- Owners: Neha (eng lead), Ben (secops lead), Priyom (product PM), Grace (CS lead).
- Deliverables & dates:
   * RFC + security checklist (Priyom) by 2027-10-27 — publish to Confluence (link below).
   * Engineering PoC (Neha) complete by 2027-11-10.
   * Internal security validation + audit export verification (Ben) complete by 2027-11-17.
   * Customer validation with Medspring (Grace) week of 2027-11-20.

I'll send a short RFC to Lauren and ask Medspring for a signed exception form for 90d retention; Grace, please coordinate the auditor contact and acceptance criteria. We'll track implementation in RDW-4591.

Meeting: I propose a 30m sync Tues 2027-10-26 to confirm RFC contents — Priyom to schedule.

Marissa
Director, Product — Security & Compliance

Related: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RDW-4591
